A real office checks one small thing. A scam collects everything, and it always sounds polite while doing it.
recap_too_good: Nothing pays a guaranteed return every month, and nothing is won in a draw you never entered. The good news is the bait.
A prize that costs you money first is not a prize. Real winnings never need a fee to come out.
If the offer is far better than anything a real office would give you, that gap is the whole trick.
Luck does not telephone people. When the good news arrives by itself, slow down and look at who is really calling.
Free money with one small condition attached is the oldest line in the book.
Good news that arrives with a fee attached has already told you what it really is.
recap_penalty_threat: Fear is the tool here. Real offices send letters and give you time, they do not threaten arrest down the phone.
No genuine officer settles a fine over a call. A threat that keeps you talking is the tell by itself.
Real trouble comes with paperwork you can read and a number you can ring back. A voice alone is not proof.
A threat is meant to stop you thinking. Put the phone down and it has nowhere left to go.
When a caller starts talking about court or arrest, the aim is panic, not justice.
Threats travel easily down a phone line because they cost nothing to make. Ask for it in writing and it disappears.
recap_official_transfer: No office, no ward and no agency asks you to move your savings into an account read out over the phone.
A safety account, a holding account, a verification account. Different names, same trap, and the money does not come back.
Real fees are paid at a counter you can walk to, not to numbers dictated on a call.
Officials never need your savings to prove anything. They already hold their own records.
If somebody with an official voice tells you where to send your money, that is the moment to hang up.
Your savings stay where they are. No safe account exists that needs your money to prove you are innocent.
shield_earned: One more shield on the wall. That is practice, not luck.
Shield earned. You will hear that voice coming next time.
Well done today. Come back tomorrow and the ear gets sharper.
That is a shield. Keep them stacking up.
Another one for the collection. Steady.
One more on the wall. Small practice, real protection.
walkthrough_intro: Let us slow down and see what would have happened next.
No harm done, this is only practice. Let us walk through it together.
That is how it catches people, and it catches sharp people too. Have a look at what was really going on.
Alright, let us rewind and look at that call properly.
Nothing lost here. Let us look at what the caller was building towards.
This is the safe place to get caught. Here is where the call was heading.
walkthrough_step_urgency: The rush was the point. Next would have come a stream of instructions while you were still catching up, with no gap to ring anyone.
Had you stayed inside that hurry, the caller would have kept the clock running right through the payment.
The next step would have been more pressure, then one small payment made while the panic was still fresh.
Going along with the countdown, you would have been kept on the line until it was done, and the checking never happens.
A real office would have let you take the day. The hurry existed to close that day down to a minute.
The hurry was there to stop the one phone call that ends this. Next would have come more of it, louder.
walkthrough_step_secrecy: Had you kept it quiet, there would have been nobody to say wait a minute. That is exactly what the secret is for.
The next step would have been a second call, still just between the two of you, and the amounts grow each time.
Keeping it from your family leaves you alone with the caller. One sentence to a daughter or a neighbour usually ends it.
Had you promised to say nothing, the caller would have come back tomorrow with a bigger favour to ask.
The silence is the plan. Next would have come a reason why telling anyone makes it worse for you.
A secret keeps every helpful person out of the room, and the next step relies on that quiet.
walkthrough_step_unusual_payment: Going along with it, you would have made one small payment first, then a bigger one to release the first.
The odd payment is the part they cannot put through an ordinary counter, so the next step always leads away from one.
The next step would have been a payment you could not stop, made in a way you have never used before.
Had you paid the way they asked, there would have been no receipt to show anyone and no counter to walk back to.
The next step always moves away from the ordinary counter, because an ordinary counter asks questions.
Going along with it, the money would have left by a route with nothing to trace and nobody to ask afterwards.
walkthrough_step_unusual_payment_voucher: Next you would have been sent downstairs for vouchers, then asked to read the codes aloud. Once those numbers are spoken, they are spent.
The next step would have been a shop downstairs, then codes read into the phone. The money, {amount} in this case, does not come back.
Going along with it, you would have bought one card, then been told a second one is needed to release the first.
The shop downstairs is the only place this works, so the next step is always the cards and never the counter.
The next step would have been a second trip downstairs, because one voucher never quite covers the fee.
Once the codes were read aloud they would have been spent, most likely before the call had even finished.
walkthrough_step_unusual_payment_courier: Next would have come a knock at the door, an envelope handed over, and somebody you cannot describe walking away with it.
The next step would have been notes counted out at your lift landing, {amount} in this case, with no receipt and nobody to ask afterwards.
Going along with it, you would have handed the cash over, and the same collector would have come back next week for more.
Cash at the door leaves no trail at all, so the next step is always somebody arriving rather than a payment you can check.
The next step would have been somebody polite arriving, taking the notes, and never being seen again.
Going along with it, a collector would have come up, and the visit would have repeated itself next month.
walkthrough_step_no_callback: Staying on the line was the goal. The next step would have been a long call with no gap for you to check anything.
Had you agreed not to ring back, there would have been no moment for a second voice to say that sounds wrong.
The next step would have been more reasons the line cannot be called, each one keeping you in the same conversation.
Going along with it, you would have been talked through everything without once dialling the number on your own card or letter.
Nobody honest fears you calling back. Next would have come a fresh excuse the moment you tried.
The next step depended on you never dialling out. One call to a number you trust would have ended the whole thing.
walkthrough_step_too_good: Going along with it, the next step would have been a small fee to release something that was never there.
The next step would have been paperwork that looks real, then one payment, then a reason why one more is needed.
The prize or the return keeps growing while the questions get quieter. That is how the good news pays for itself.
Had the offer been taken up, the first payment would have been small and the second one much less small.
A win you never entered and a return nobody else gets are the same promise, and both need your money first.
The next step would have been a fee to release a prize that only ever existed on this call.
walkthrough_step_detail_fishing: Once those details were read out, the caller would not have needed you again. The next call would have been to your bank, with somebody else answering every question as if they were you.
The next step would have been one more harmless question, then another, until the form was complete.
Your name, your card numbers and the code sent to your phone are the whole set. With them an account opens without you.
Had you answered, the details would have been used quietly, and the first sign would have been a message you did not expect.
Real staff already hold what they need to check you, so the next question would have been the one they actually wanted.
The next step would have been silence, then somebody using your name in a place you have never been.
walkthrough_step_penalty_threat: The threat was there to keep you moving. Next would have come a way to make it all go away, and it would have cost money.
Had the fear taken hold, the caller would have offered a settlement on the spot, payable right now.
A real case gives you a letter, a reference and time. The next step here would have been paying to stop something that was never happening.
Going along with it, you would have paid to avoid a court date that does not exist.
Nobody is arrested over the telephone. The next words would have been the amount that makes it stop.
The next step would have been a price for making the trouble disappear, and the trouble was never real.
walkthrough_step_official_transfer: The next step would have been an account number read out slowly, and a walk to the machine while still on the phone.
Had the money moved into that safe account, it would have been out of reach within minutes.
A holding account, a safety account, a verification account. Whatever the name, the next step is always your money leaving your side.
Going along with it, that transfer, {amount} in this case, would have landed with strangers who opened the account this morning.
No office asks you to move savings by phone. The next step would have been a receipt that helps nobody.
The next step would have been you at the machine, still on the phone, sending money that never comes back.
